versions.changelog:
Documentation and packaging only, answering the scan findings against 1.1.0. No behaviour changed, no feature was added or removed, and the test suite is unchanged at 1371 passing offline.

The design record and implementation plan no longer ship inside the skill. They remain in git history, reachable at tag v1.1.0 and through pull request 24. A scanner reads a shipped document as live guidance, so a historical record of a defect that was found and fixed reads as a current one, and a historical plan's example trigger phrases read as routing instructions.

A real account's identifiers are out of the published tree. The project id, request and deployment ids, invocation id, domains and route names in the example output and in the recorded API row were replaced with fictional values of the same shape. What made those examples worth having is preserved: they are still real captured output, the field names and types and empty strings in the recorded row are still exactly as the API returned them, and each block now says whether it was captured and redacted or is illustrative.

Token setup leads with the route that does not store the secret. The reference form is the primary recommendation in both the README and the setup guide, the inline paste and the plaintext config file are labelled as fallbacks, and each carries its warning immediately beside it: a token pasted on a command line reaches shell history and process listings, and one written into openclaw.json is a secret at rest that backups copy, so it wants restrictive file permissions and the least-privileged read scope Vercel allows.

Three disclosures moved to where a reader cannot miss them. A provider error message is quoted verbatim on purpose and can carry operational context, so it belongs to the person who asked rather than to another service. An application log line can contain that application's own secrets or personal data: this client scrubs the one token it holds and nothing can distinguish anyone else's secret from ordinary text, so quoted log output should be the minimum that answers the question. And the generic metric surface reaches every metric an account-scoped token can see, not only the web vitals, which is a reason to scope the token narrowly.

A third surface: request logs. The skill could report how many people came and how fast the site felt, and could not answer the question people actually ask in a hurry, which is what broke. Now it can: vercel-insights errors --since 30m.

Three presets, all read-only: errors (failing requests, newest first), logs (the same table without the error filter), and error-summary (the same errors tallied by status, by route and by exact message). Nine logs-only flags: --level, --status-code, --source, --method, --search, --request-id, --branch, --deployment and --expand.

An error is a 5xx response, a crashed function, or a request that logged an error or fatal line, so errors issues two queries and merges them by request id. That is the design rather than caution: on this API level matches what a request printed and statusCode matches what it answered, so a 500 that crashed without printing is invisible to one and a 200 whose handler logged a stack trace is invisible to the other.

The default window is 1 hour, not the global 7 days, because runtime logs are retained for one hour on Hobby and one day on Pro. A 7 day default would report nothing and read as a healthy site. An empty result says so and prints the retention limits rather than implying nothing failed.

Two changes alter what an existing command does. --budget on a traffic preset now exits 2 instead of being silently ignored: it was only ever wired into the Speed Insights emitter, so a CI job using it with a traffic preset had been exiting 0 and protecting nothing. And four cross-surface refusal messages were reworded, which matters only to a script matching on their text.

The read-only allowlist grows from five entries to six, the new one a GET on vercel.com rather than api.vercel.com. That is forced: Vercel's documented runtime-logs endpoint is an endless stream that never sends response headers, and counting 5xx through the observability metrics API answers 402 Observability Plus is required. The endpoint that works is the one vercel logs itself calls. docs/api-notes.md records every probe behind that conclusion and says plainly that this one endpoint is CLI-verified rather than OpenAPI-documented and can change without notice.

Request logs are the first surface that prints text a response supplied rather than numbers the tool computed, so two things were added to keep old promises true: every log message and path is escaped before printing, and the client scrubs its own access token out of log rows during normalization, upstream of the verbatim row that --json emits. Nothing can tell a user's own secret from ordinary text, so no general redaction is claimed.

Test suite 1080 to 1371 tests, all offline. ruff and mypy --strict clean. No new runtime dependency.

Security: raises the requests dependency floor from >=2.28 to >=2.33.0, past every published advisory for the package, the newest being GHSA-gc5v-m9x4-r6x2 (insecure temporary file reuse in extract_zipped_paths). This is a security floor rather than a feature floor; nothing in the codebase needs an API newer than 2.28. The supported Python range is unchanged, since requests 2.33.0 declares requires-python >=3.10 exactly as this project does. No code changes. The suite was run against requests==2.33.0 specifically: 1080 passed.

Documentation release. The setup instructions now open by asking which kind of reader they have, and route OpenClaw users through a four step walkthrough that states what should appear after each step. Fixes two blockers that stop a fresh install from running: clawhub install does not preserve the executable bit, and requests is absent from most system interpreters. No behaviour changes, and no change to what the tool can reach.

First published release. Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights from one command line: 19 presets, project discovery, performance budgets, and any observability metric by id. Read-only against a five-endpoint allowlist.
